## Definition

Flag debt is the operational and technical burden created by feature flags that remain in code after their rollout is complete and the feature has been stabilized. These "zombie" flags are never removed, creating what appears to be a permanent fixture of the codebase but actually represents dead code under ongoing test burden.

## The Core Problem

Every inactive flag effectively multiplies the number of code paths the system must maintain and test. A single flag introduces two paths: one with the flag enabled, one disabled. Multiple dormant flags compound this exponentially:

- 1 flag = 2 possible states
- 2 flags = 4 possible states
- 3 flags = 8 possible states
- 10 flags = 1,024 possible states

The test matrix grows silently. Most of these combinations are never reached in production (the flag is always off, or always on), but they still exist in the code and demand coverage.

## Why Flags Don't Get Cleaned Up

Removing a flag is often treated as a non-urgent task that slips in priority:

- The feature is already live and working; removal adds no business value
- No single person is accountable for the cleanup
- The work feels low-risk and gets deferred in favor of new features
- Time-to-live (TTL) policies are rarely enforced on flags

## Cleanup Discipline

Effective flag management requires treating cleanup as part of the feature lifecycle:

**Explicit lifecycle management:**
- Every flag should have a target removal date set at creation time
- Removal is a scheduled, documented maintenance task, not an optional cleanup
- The flag owner is responsible for ensuring removal before the deadline

**Automated enforcement:**
- Flags should raise warnings or errors if they exceed their TTL
- CI/CD pipelines can fail builds if dormant flags are detected
- Code review automation can flag new flags without a removal date

**Testing discipline:**
- Do not consider a feature "done" until the flag is removed
- Acceptance criteria should include flag cleanup
- Test only the enabled state once the flag is removed (no longer maintaining the disabled path)

## Related Patterns

Cleanup discipline is closely related to [[concepts/technical-debt]] management broadly — flag debt is a specific, high-impact form of it that tends to be overlooked because individual flags seem harmless.
